WV9-P01.5.note: The author lines up ironies (eleven blank days matching Ida's, a notice promising an end to the walk hung beside the walkers' rota), a wry, amused stance; a pointed 'critical' reading of the council is defensible.

WV9-P03.5.note: The narrator stacks up threats (frost Friday, no oil until Monday, no helpers, Tomas coughing) and ends on the far row 'where the cold would settle', which reads as worry; a wistful farewell from the train is a weaker second reading.
